story.title: Every validator code can be looked up
story.source_text: When validate.py reports a code like BRF009 there is nowhere to look it up: 55 of the 153 codes the validator and batch.py can emit are documented in no reference file, so a maintainer or an implementer reading a finding has to open the validator source. Add `validate.py --codes` that lists every code with the phase it belongs to and what it means, generate references/codes.md from it, and make selftest's docs-consistency suite fail when a code can be emitted that codes.md does not list, so the index cannot rot. Maintainers only; nothing changes for someone running the validator today.
story.summary_human: A finding like BRF009 is currently a dead end unless you open validate.py: 56 of 160 codes are documented nowhere. This adds an explicit registry of every code with a one-line meaning, a `--codes` flag (plain, JSON, markdown), a generated `references/codes.md`, a row for it in SKILL.md, and four selftest checks: emitted equals registered both ways, severity matches the call sites, the file is current, and each meaning is a meaning. Two subtasks, one repo, one day and a half.
story.technical_notes_human: Emitters are validate.py, batch.py and criteria.py (AC012 is criteria's alone, `criteria.py:106`); summary.py and selftest.py contain code literals as consumers, not emitters. 'Emitted' is mechanical: a code literal as first argument of error/warn/report/add or as a `("ERROR"|"WARN", "CODE", ...)` tuple in criteria.py - which is how DOD001, emitted via an alias at `validate.py:1129`, is counted. D1: explicit per-module `CODES` dicts, `"CODE": (severity, meaning)`; dict-key syntax is what keeps the dead-entry check from matching the registry itself. D2: codes.md committed, selftest asserts LF-normalised equality. D3: `PHASE_OF["BAT"] = "9 batch"`. D5: output sorted by phase label then code, like main()'s own grouping. D6: --codes dispatches before the bundle is opened; --json under --codes emits a list. The existing docs regex `[A-Z]{3,6}` skips AC/DT - S2 widens it to `{2,6}`. SKILL.md:843 still says 'six suites'; S2 fixes it with the reference-table row.

decisions.question: Where does the meaning of a code come from?

options.label: Regex-extract the message template from each rep.error/warn call
options.tradeoff: no new source of truth; templates are %-format prose over several lines and read badly; no way to detect a dead entry

options.label: An explicit CODES dict per module with a one-line meaning
options.tradeoff: one more thing to maintain; but a set both directions of the selftest can compare

decisions.chosen: An explicit CODES dict per module with a one-line meaning
decisions.rationale: A reader wants the condition, not the message; and the both-ways check in AC3 needs a set whose literals are syntactically distinct from call sites - dict keys are.

decisions.question: Is codes.md committed, or generated at test time?

options.label: Generated by selftest, never committed
options.tradeoff: cannot rot; but unreadable in the repo or an installed skill without running Python

options.label: Committed, with selftest asserting it equals the generator's output
options.tradeoff: one regeneration step per code change; readable everywhere

decisions.chosen: Committed, with selftest asserting it equals the generator's output
decisions.rationale: The skill is installed as plain files and read by agents that may not run scripts; a committed file is the only one they see.

decisions.question: Where do batch.py's BAT codes sit in the phase grouping, and with which label?

options.label: Leave them; phase_of returns '9 other'
options.tradeoff: nothing to change; five codes land in a bucket named 'other'

options.label: Add BAT to PHASE_OF as its own group
options.tradeoff: one dict entry; the grouping in validate.py output changes for nobody, since batch codes never appear there

decisions.chosen: Add BAT to PHASE_OF as its own group
decisions.rationale: 'other' is where meaning goes to die. Label '9 batch': the batch check runs before the push, alongside emit. A validation run never emits BAT, so main()'s grouped output is unchanged.

decisions.question: Which scripts count as emitters, and how does --codes reach their registries?

options.label: validate.py and batch.py only
options.tradeoff: misses AC012, which criteria.py alone emits - a code --codes would call invented

options.label: validate.py, batch.py, criteria.py; --codes imports the other two lazily
options.tradeoff: one lazy import inside the handler; neither module imports validate, so no cycle

decisions.chosen: validate.py, batch.py, criteria.py; --codes imports the other two lazily
decisions.rationale: criteria.py:106 emits through a findings list; the archaeologist re-opened it. Consumers (summary.py, selftest.py) are excluded by the mechanical definition of 'emitted'.

decisions.question: What does --codes print, and in which order?

options.label: Reuse main()'s grouped print loop (phase header, indented items)
options.tradeoff: no new format; but a header per phase and indented lines make grep-by-code impossible and the byte gate fragile

options.label: One TSV line per code, sorted by (phase label, code); --markdown groups under headings in the same order; --json a list
options.tradeoff: a second output style; but one line per code is what a lookup and a diff both want

decisions.chosen: One TSV line per code, sorted by (phase label, code); --markdown groups under headings in the same order; --json a list
decisions.rationale: PHASE_OF insertion order is not phase order (ENB, BAS sit after IRR); sorting by label is the ordering main() already uses, and it is the only one two implementers would reproduce identically.

decisions.question: Where is the severity column from, given ten codes emitted at both severities and DOD001 whose severity a config rule decides?

options.label: Authored in the registry, unchecked
options.tradeoff: a wrong 'error' on a warn-only code is published and never caught

options.label: Authored in the registry, and selftest compares it to the call sites: error | warn | 'error | warn' | 'config' for an aliased emitter
options.tradeoff: one more check; the column is then trustworthy

decisions.chosen: Authored in the registry, and selftest compares it to the call sites: error | warn | 'error | warn' | 'config' for an aliased emitter
decisions.rationale: The tester found the column would be wrong for ten codes with nothing able to fail. Codes are never split - REV009 and PND001 are cited in existing findings.
